title: Con todo: matizar una conclusión sin negarla del todo

sections.content: Con todo (even so, all the same, nevertheless) softens or qualifies a point without fully reversing it -- useful for balanced closing assessments that want to hold an achievement and a limitation together. It typically opens a new sentence or clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Con todo, el comercio entre los propios países latinoamericanos seguía representando una proporción relativamente modesta del total.
items.english: Even so, trade among the Latin American countries themselves still represented a relatively modest share of the total.

items.spanish: Con todo, estos logros institucionales no debían subestimarse.
items.english: All the same, these institutional achievements shouldn't be underestimated.

items.spanish: Con todo, el sueño bolivariano de una Latinoamérica unida seguía tan lejos de concretarse como antes.
items.english: Even so, the Bolivarian dream of a united Latin America remained as far from being realized as before.

items.spanish: El proyecto tuvo dificultades reales; con todo, logró avanzar más de lo que muchos habían anticipado.
items.english: The project faced real difficulties; even so, it managed to advance further than many had anticipated.

sections.content: Con todo works similarly to aun así, but leans slightly more toward acknowledging real limitations before reaffirming a point's continued validity -- it's a natural fit for balanced, on-the-other-hand closing paragraphs.
